name: Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome

criteria.description: Symptoms of proximal intestinal obstruction (postprandial epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, weight loss)
Imaging evidence of duodenal compression between SMA and aorta (aortomesenteric angle < 25 degrees or aortomesenteric distance < 8 mm on CT/MRI)
Dilation of first and second portions of duodenum with abrupt cutoff at third portion
Relief of symptoms with positional changes (left lateral decubitus or prone)
Predisposing factor: rapid weight loss, spinal surgery/casting, high insertion of ligament of Treitz

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Compatible symptoms plus imaging showing reduced aortomesenteric angle (<25 degrees) or distance (<8 mm) with duodenal compression. Other causes of duodenal obstruction must be excluded.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Often a diagnosis of exclusion. May coexist with nutcracker syndrome (left renal vein compression by the same mechanism).

pathognomonic.notes: Relieved by prone or left lateral decubitus position
Bile-stained vomiting due to duodenal obstruction

searchTerms: side pain in back or abdomen

rare.symptomName: Acute gastric dilation with risk of necrosis
searchTerms: stomach swelling with risk of tissue death

laboratory: Electrolyte abnormalities from protracted vomiting (hypokalemic, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis)
imaging: CT angiography: aortomesenteric angle < 25° (normal 38-65°) and distance < 8 mm (normal 10-28 mm)
Upper GI series: abrupt vertical cutoff in third portion of duodenum with proximal dilation
MRA can demonstrate the same findings as CTA without radiation
other: Upper endoscopy to exclude intrinsic duodenal obstruction
Hypotonic duodenography may show extrinsic compression
Positional relief (Hayes maneuver: left lateral decubitus) supports diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Gastroparesis shows delayed gastric emptying on scintigraphy
No duodenal compression on imaging in gastroparesis
MALS involves celiac artery compression, not duodenal
MALS shows celiac artery stenosis on CTA
CIPO lacks the specific SMA-aorta angle narrowing

redFlags: Acute massive gastric dilation (risk of gastric necrosis/perforation)
Severe electrolyte derangements from intractable vomiting
Concurrent left renal vein compression (nutcracker syndrome)
references: Welsch T, et al. Recalling superior mesenteric artery syndrome. Dig Surg. 2007;24(3):149-156.
Merrett ND, et al. Superior mesenteric artery syndrome: diagnosis and treatment strategies. J Gastrointest Surg. 2009;13(2):287-292.
Scovell S, et al. Superior mesenteric artery syndrome. UpToDate. 2024.
